title: SLO tradeoff matrix and cross-team decision digest
content:
Purpose: Capture a compact, action-oriented tradeoff matrix for proposed SLOs and surface binding decisions for cross-functional stakeholders (product, infra, runtime, customer success, and sales). This doc is the single source for the set of agreed tradeoffs for the November 2026 reliability cadence and the experimental canary in December.

Background: During Q3 we ran three parallel SLO experiments (chat latency targets, embedding throughput commits, and cold-start tail coverage). There is still disagreement across teams about how tight targets should be vs. the expected cost uplift on Dedicated and Hosted tiers. Product wants a conservative customer-facing promise; infra wants headroom for graceful degradation and cost predictability; runtime asks for permissive thresholds to optimize batching. This digest distills the options and records a mutually acceptable decision path with explicit rollback and measurement windows.

Scope: Service surface: Text generation (chat) and embeddings API routes; traffic classes: interactive (p95 target), background embeddings batch (throughput SLO), and cold/warm-start tail (p99). Not in scope: model quality targets (handled separately by Eval team).

Key objectives: 
- Finalize binding SLO targets for interactive chat (p95) and embeddings throughput by 2026-11-15.
- Define latency budget allocation (edge, routing, runtime) per request class.
- Agree cost guardrail thresholds and an automatic fallback policy.
- Create a 30/60/90 day experiment window and measurement plan for canary.

Decision owners and approvers: 
- Primary owner: Aisha Patel (SRE lead)
- Product approver: Elena Rodriguez (product-hosted-api)
- Runtime approver: Marco Chen (serving-runtime)
- Infra approver: Samir Gupta (platform-engineering)
- CS stakeholder: Priya Kapoor (customer-success)
- Exec reviewer: Ben Thompson (VP Eng)

Tradeoff matrix (compact): Each row is a decision that must be approved or sent back for rework. Columns: Option A (Aggressive SLO), Option B (Balanced), Option C (Conservative SLO); Expected cost delta vs. baseline (hosted), Risk to feature SLAs, Operational complexity, Rollout tempo.

1) Interactive chat p95 target
- Option A: 80ms p95 across regions. Cost delta: +45% (GPU hours), Risk: high (may require pre-warming, denser allocation), Complexity: high, Rollout: slow (8–12 wks canary).
- Option B: 150ms p95. Cost delta: +18%, Risk: moderate, Complexity: moderate, Rollout: medium (4–6 wks canary).
- Option C: 250ms p95. Cost delta: +2%, Risk: low, Complexity: low, Rollout: fast (2–3 wks).

Binding decision 1: Approve Option B as the target for hosted and Dedicated standard tier, with Option A reserved for premium Dedicated customers and experimental bounded regions. Rationale: balances product expectations and cost. Action owner: Product + Runtime to finalize capacity plan by 2026-10-01.

2) Embeddings throughput SLO (tokens/sec per instance / aggregate qps)
- Option A: 99th percentile throughput guarantee for reserved pools. Cost delta: +30% reserved capacity, Risk: moderate, Complexity: requires autoscaler policy changes.
- Option B: 95th percentile with soft SLA and autoscale window tuning. Cost delta: +10%, Risk: low-moderate, Complexity: moderate.
- Option C: Best-effort throughput with burst credits. Cost delta: negligible, Risk: higher for heavy enterprise batch jobs, Complexity: low.

Binding decision 2: Approve Option B for standard Dedicated and hosted; Option A for Reserved Enterprise (sales-committed) only. Action owner: Infra + Sales to update offering SKUs and billing by 2026-10-15.

3) Cold-start tail (p99): coverage and mitigation
- Option A: Proactive KV-cache warming and persistent warm pool to achieve p99 < 800ms. Cost delta: +20%, Complexity: moderate-high.
- Option B: Opportunistic prefetch on high-risk routes + aggressive caching to hit p99 < 1.5s. Cost delta: +6%, Complexity: moderate.
- Option C: No change (accept higher p99 up to 3s) with clear documentation to CS. Cost delta: 0%, Complexity: low.

Binding decision 3: Approve Option B with a fallthrough to Option A for premium enterprise customers. Measurement: define a cold-start metric (cold_request_p99) and instrument for 2 weeks prior to canary. Action owner: Runtime + Observability to deliver instrumentation by 2026-09-22.

Latency budget allocation (breakdown guidance): For interactive chat p95=150ms target -> network+edge: <=30ms, routing/proxy: <=20ms, runtime inference (token generation tail): <=80ms + buffer 20ms. Teams to baseline current split and submit variance doc by 2026-09-28.

Cost guardrails and automatic fallback policy: 
- Hard budget trigger: if marginal per-token cost for Hosted increases above 22% vs. baseline for 72h, then automatic fallback to a slightly lower-quality quantized model variant (quant2) for non-premium requests.
- Soft alarm: 15% cost increase triggers paging rota and manual review.
- Billing gating: Sales must accept that Reserved Enterprise SKUs may include a higher cost attachment (Option A) communicated in the contract.

Rollout plan and experiment windows: 
- Week 0 (baseline measurement): 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-14 gather p95/p99 baselines and cold-start samples.
- Canary window 1 (small traffic): 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-29 route 3% traffic to new config (Option B). Monitor health, SLI deltas, cost deltas.
- Canary window 2 (scale-up): 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-13 route 25% traffic.
- Full rollout gate: decision meeting 2026-11-15. If canary meets SLI gates AND cost guardrails, proceed; else iterate.

Measurement plan and SLI definitions: 
- p95_latency_chat (region, route_tag): measured at edge egress in ms, sample rate 100%.
- embeddings_throughput_ratio: percent of requests meeting throughput SLO over 1h windows.
- cold_request_p99: p99 for requests flagged as cold by KV cache TTL or instance uptime.
- per_token_cost_delta: delta vs rolling 30d baseline, aggregated daily.

Gating criteria for canary success (all must pass): 
- p95 latency delta <= +10% relative to baseline for canary population.
- p99 cold tail delta <= +12% relative to baseline.
- per_token_cost_delta <= soft alarm threshold (15%) for canary population for any 24h window.
- Error rate (5xxs) increase < 0.2% absolute.

Communication and runbook: 
- Daily 15-minute canary sync with SRE, Runtime, Infra, Product, CS during canary windows. Slack channel #slo-canary-stream.
- Escalation path: on any gate breach -> immediate paging of SRE primary -> convene 15-min triage -> if degradation persists >30 min, rollback to previous config.
- Postmortem template: timeline, root cause hypothesis, corrective actions, owners, and preventive signals.

Open questions and follow-ups (action items): 
- Q1: Should we include a separate SLO tier for high-frequency low-latency interactive tests used by internal QA? Owner: Product. Due: 2026-09-30.
- Q2: Confirm storage/eviction semantics for KV warming across regions (affects cold_start metric). Owner: Runtime. Due: 2026-09-22.
- Q3: Autoscaler policy changes required for embeddings guaranteed throughput (evaluate min-instance delta). Owner: Infra. Due: 2026-10-05.

Appendix: Quick reference of metrics dashboards to review during canary: 
- Chat latency dashboard: OBS/Latency/Chat-p95 (filter: region, tier)
- Embeddings throughput playback: OBS/Throughput/Embeddings-p95-p99
- Cost delta dashboard: FIN/Cost/Per-Token-Delta (hosted vs baseline)

Meeting cadence to finalize decisions: 
- Decision sync (1hr): weekly on Mondays until 2026-11-15. Required attendees: owners + approvers.
- Daily canary standup (15m): during canary windows.
- Exec review (30m): 2026-11-15 for go/no-go.

Notes to reviewers: This digest is intentionally terse and decision-focused. If any approver cannot accept the binding decisions above, please reply with an explicit counter-proposal and data rationale by 2026-09-24 so we can incorporate into the next decision sync.

Signed: Aisha Patel (SRE lead)
Revision log: 2026-09-14 created initial draft; 2026-09-22 added cold-start instrumentation action; 2026-10-02 updated canary windows and finalized binding decision 1.
